title: Skill: epic definition of done as [A<n>] items, not one prose sentence
description:
SKILL.md 'Epic definition of done' gives a single prose --acceptance as its example. [A<n>]-marked items are documented only for PROJECTS (goal-design.md). But acceptance is consumed item by item: [evidence.acceptance] maps A<n> ids to commands, and ticfac (a consumer runner) addresses epic acceptance by item id — its runconfig refuses an id that is not A<n> 'as written in the tick's acceptance criteria', and its defect-absorption rule (ticfac gvc/pzp) names WHICH item a finding makes unreachable, and refuses to absorb when the epic states no done. A prose done cannot be addressed that way.

Change: make [A<n>]-marked lines the default shape for an epic's --acceptance, with an example; say each item is either RUNNABLE (names the command that proves it) or not-yet-runnable (checked by prediction/judgement, and says so); keep the existing A<n> uniqueness rule across epic and project.
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md's epic DoD section and its example use [A<n>] items; the runnable vs not-yet-runnable distinction is stated; tk-commands/goal-design references agree with it; no example in the skill shows an epic DoD as a single prose sentence
